thread:
Sasha: heads-up — saw steady memory growth on the kv-slab rotation path while running the long-context regression suite. repro attached below. :eyes:

Sasha: run command:
```
./tools/bench_kv --suite long-context --workers 8 --seq-len 65536 --duration 1200 
# baseline: ~2.1GB resident after 20m, current run: ~3.8GB and climbing
```

Matt: @Sasha can you capture a heap/profile around 5-10min? sounds like fragmentation or pages not getting returned to OS.

Sasha: pasted the flame-ish summary from the perf capture (sampling, 10s window at ~8m):
```
kv_slab_alloc: 48%
kv_page_rotate: 22%
kv_reuse_check: 6%
malloc: 14%
other: 10%
```

Priya: interesting — rotation & alloc dominating. do we have metrics for "free pages" vs "active pages" during run?

Sasha: quick telemetry dump (every 60s sample):
```
time   free_pages  active_pages  slab_frag_pct  reclaimed_count  total_pages
0m60   1200        4300          18             140              5500
0m120  1180        4380          21             130              5560
0m180  1150        4465          25             90               5615
0m240  1110        4550          28             45               5660
```

Alex: that pattern screams delayed reclamation — reclaimed_count falling while active_pages rising. could be the rotation cursor skipping some slabs because of concurrent refill logic. saw a similar signal in a different cluster a while back.

Matt: any recent changes to freelist handling or rotation heuristics? last green commit was 176f3a2 which tweaked rotation to favor contiguous eviction.

Priya: yeah 176f3a2 introduced the "don’t touch slab while active_write" guard. Might be safe but could leave slabs stranded if writes keep bouncing slots.

Sasha: reproduced with a synthetic pattern that toggles writes across prefixes (makes many cold->hot transitions). added repro flag --hot-sweep. results show reclaimed_count drop to single digits after ~6m.

Sasha: quick hack test: disabled the active_write guard locally and mem stable at ~2.2GB. not a solution but confirms guard blocks reclamation.

Alex: can we add a fast-path to allow rotation when an older epoch indicates no pending writers? i.e., check per-slab epoch vs global epoch and rotate if older.

Priya: also consider moving some of the rotation to background GC thread that can steal slabs when memory pressure high. avoids latency hit on hot request path.

Matt: agrees. but we should be careful about contention — background GC will need lightweight probes to avoid stalling. maybe exponential backoff between tries.

infra-bot: CI run kv-longcontext-regression #482 failed on perf threshold (mem-growth slope +0.9MB/min > allowed 0.2MB/min) — logs: https://ci.internal/reports/482 (bench artifact attached) :bug:

Sasha: opened draft PR with naive fix (epoch-check + force-rotate-on-pressure) — link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/2345 (WIP). bench results in PR description.

Priya: can you include microbench that toggles guard on/off and measure reclaimed_count and page churn? want numbers for the tradeoff matrix.

Sasha: will add. initial microbench shows reclaimed_count 140->420/min when guard disabled; latency p99 up by ~0.5ms in synthetic worst-case.

Alex: acceptable if we gate behind config and enable background GC; prefer incremental approach: 1) epoch check fast-path, 2) background GC, 3) revisit guard semantics.

Matt: assigning owner to Sasha for a short-term mitigation, Priya for design of GC thread. please add test vectors to the long-context suite:
- pattern: prefix-toggle-hot (simulates many write toggles)
- pattern: append-only (baseline)
- pattern: bursty-hotspots

Sasha: added tests to repo under tests/kv/long_context_patterns, pushed to bench infra. CI will pick them up next run.

Priya: also request flamegraph from a run where guard is enabled vs disabled, to validate rotation callers.

Sasha: attached two sampling flame snapshots (links):
- https://artifacts.internal/kv/guard-enabled-8m.svg
- https://artifacts.internal/kv/guard-disabled-8m.svg

Matt: nice. next steps: review PR 2345, add background GC design doc, and bake new test patterns into perf-gate. i'll schedule a quick sync tomorrow 10am PT. :calendar:

Alex: thanks team — great repro and telemetry. if anyone wants to triage offline ping me. :thumbsup:

Sasha: merging WIP after tests green on branch with feature-flag default off. will iterate. :party:
